motivation: To develop a rigorous mathematical framework for supersymmetric vertex algebras using factorization algebras, extending Costello–Gwilliam's work to the supersymmetric setting.
method: Introduces SUSY factorization algebras on embedded SUSY disks with symmetry conditions and proves a SUSY analogue of the Costello–Gwilliam extraction theorem.
result: For linear targets, obtains the free β-γ system; for general complex targets, identifies the resulting SUSY vertex algebra with the chiral de Rham complex; shows Ricci-flat Kähler and hyperkähler targets give N=1 and N=2 supersymmetric enhancements.
conclusion: Provides a new construction of SUSY vertex algebras and connects them to geometric targets, with implications for supersymmetric field theories and string theory.

title: Direct Reconstruction For Acoustic Inverse Born Scattering
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the inverse medium scattering problem for the Helmholtz equation in two dimensions, i.e., the task to recover a compactly supported penetrable two-dimensional scatterer from full knowledge of the associated far field data or, equivalently, the far field operator. Although this problem is uniquely solvable, it is severely ill-posed and nonlinear. In the regime of weak scattering, the Born approximation yields a linearized relation between the contrast and the far field data, thus overcoming the second difficulty. This linear setting allows to build on recent work on linearized electrical impedance tomography, which relies on triangular Zernike decompositions, to derive an explicit reconstruction formula that expresses the expansion coefficients of the contrast in terms of those of the far field data. By choosing the expansion functions appropriately, the resulting system matrix decouples into separate (infinite) triangular systems for the spatial angular frequencies in the contrast. Consequently, each of these systems can be solved independently by performing forward substitutions. Our numerical experiments indicate that this approach, combined with an adequate regularization method, remains effective even when applied to full nonlinear far field data beyond the Born regime.
tldr: This paper presents a direct reconstruction method for the acoustic inverse Born scattering problem using triangular Zernike decompositions.
motivation: To overcome the nonlinearity and ill-posedness of the inverse medium scattering problem for the Helmholtz equation.
method: The Born approximation linearizes the problem, then triangular Zernike decompositions are used to derive an explicit reconstruction formula that decouples the system into independent triangular systems solved by forward substitution.
result: Numerical experiments show the method remains effective even beyond the Born regime with appropriate regularization.
conclusion: The approach provides a fast, direct reconstruction method for acoustic scattering, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Search-Time Contamination In Deep Research Agents: Measuring Performance Inflation In Public Benchmark Evaluation
authors: Yongjie Wang, Xinyue Zhang, Kunhong Yao, Zhiwei Zeng, Kaisong Song, Jun Lin, Zhiqi Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public benchmarks enable fair and reproducible evaluation of LLM reasoning, but they become fragile for deep research agents that actively search the web during inference. Such agents may retrieve public benchmark metadata, question context, or even ground-truth answers via web search. This gives rise to Search-Time Contamination (STC), where external retrieval bypasses intended reasoning and inflates measured performance. We systematically study STC in deep research agent evaluation. We define three contamination types with increasing severity, namely Benchmark Metadata Leakage, Question-Context Leakage, and Explicit Answer Leakage, and develop detection algorithms to identify them and quantify their impact on agent performance. Evaluating modern deep research agents on six public benchmarks, we find that STC is widespread and can inflate performance by up to 4%. Our findings show that existing evaluations may overestimate true reasoning ability. We therefore advocate contamination-aware practices, including isolated sandboxes, transparent search trajectories, and controlled benchmark access.
tldr: This paper studies how deep research agents can inflate their benchmark performance by retrieving answers via web search during inference, a phenomenon called Search-Time Contamination.
motivation: Public benchmarks are widely used to evaluate LLM reasoning, but deep research agents that search the web during inference may inadvertently access benchmark data, leading to overestimated performance.
method: The authors define three types of contamination (metadata leakage, question-context leakage, explicit answer leakage) and develop detection algorithms to identify and quantify contamination in six public benchmarks.
result: Search-Time Contamination is widespread and can inflate performance by up to 4% in modern deep research agents.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for contamination-aware evaluation practices such as isolated sandboxes, transparent search trajectories, and controlled benchmark access.

title: Should Demand Models Incorporate Competitor Prices? Oblivious Learning And Algorithmic Collusion
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a platform with many sellers, should a pricing algorithm explicitly model competitors' prices when learning demand? Classical learning arguments suggest an affirmative answer: ignoring competitors induces model misspecification and inefficiency. In contrast, recent work on algorithmic collusion suggests that strategic obliviousness -- deliberately ignoring competitor prices -- may facilitate collusive outcomes and improve profits. We study this modeling choice in a stylized competitive market with unknown noisy demand, in which multiple sellers repeatedly set prices and estimate demand via iterated least squares, and either incorporate competitors' prices into their demand models (informed) or ignore them (oblivious). We first show that, relative to a monopolist, an oblivious seller in a competitive market must explore more aggressively to compensate for the loss of dynamic competitor information. Building on this insight, we characterize market dynamics when all sellers are oblivious and show that prices converge to the competitive outcome under sufficient exploration, while a continuum of pseudo-equilibria arises when exploration decays. Analyzing the resulting price trajectories, we uncover an excursion phenomenon that gives rise to transient collusive patterns that dissipate as learning progresses. In markets with both oblivious and informed sellers, the informed strictly out-earn the oblivious. Read as a strategy game, the modeling choice has a unique Nash equilibrium: the all-informed market, in which prices converge to the competitive outcome efficiently. Overall, our results indicate that collusive patterns are not robust and are not sustained by oblivious modeling; therefore, incorporating competitor information, together with sufficient price exploration, remains a reliable strategy for sellers in competitive markets.
tldr: This paper studies whether pricing algorithms should incorporate competitor prices in a competitive market, finding that informed models outperform oblivious ones and collusive patterns are not robust.
motivation: To resolve the tension between classical learning arguments favoring informed models and recent work suggesting obliviousness may facilitate collusion.
method: The authors model a stylized competitive market with multiple sellers using iterated least squares to estimate demand, comparing oblivious (ignore competitor prices) and informed (incorporate competitor prices) sellers.
result: Oblivious sellers must explore more aggressively; all-oblivious markets converge to competitive outcomes under sufficient exploration but exhibit transient collusive patterns; informed sellers strictly out-earn oblivious ones; the unique Nash equilibrium is the all-informed market.
conclusion: Incorporating competitor information with sufficient price exploration is a reliable strategy; collusive patterns from obliviousness are not robust and dissipate with learning.

title: Willing But Unable: Separating Refusal From Capability In Code LLMs Via Abliteration
authors: Cristina Carleo, Pietro Liguori, Naghmeh Ivaki, Domenico Cotroneo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Producing a labeled vulnerable code at scale is a recurring obstacle for learning-based vulnerability detection: mined corpora carry substantial label noise, and existing LLM-based augmentation propagates these inaccuracies because it transforms vulnerable seeds rather than synthesising vulnerabilities from a specification. A complementary route is to start from safe code and ask an instruction-tuned LLM to inject a specified CWE (which would shift the labeling burden from open-ended detection to bounded binary confirmation) but safety-aligned code LLMs systematically refuse such prompts. This paper is a preliminary feasibility study of abliteration, a low-rank weight edit that orthogonally projects out the refusal direction in the residual stream, as a tool to remove this barrier. We use Python and CWE-89 (SQL injection) as a case study, evaluating the Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct family at 3B, 7B, and 14B parameters on safe samples drawn from PromSec and SafeCoder, replicated three times per condition. We find that (i) refusal on injection prompts is strongly size- and prompt-context-dependent: the 14B refuses 100% of prompts, the 7B refuses 73% of PromSec but only 5% of SafeCoder, whereas the 3B is essentially never blocked; (ii) abliteration reduces refusal to zero or near-zero across all sizes while leaving syntactic validity above 93%, supporting the view that, in this setting, refusal can be detached from measured code-generation capability; and (iii) the post-abliteration injection rate remains capacity-bound (88-97% on the 14B, 89-90% on the 7B, and 25-48% on the 3B) separating willingness, which abliteration unlocks, from capability, which scales with parameters. Vulnerability verdicts are produced by a three-tool detector ensemble (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit) followed by manual adjudication by two authors on detector-positive outputs.
tldr: This paper explores abliteration, a weight-editing technique to bypass safety alignment in code LLMs for generating vulnerable code, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: To enable instruction-tuned code LLMs to inject specific vulnerabilities (e.g., SQL injection) for generating labeled vulnerable code at scale, overcoming refusal due to safety alignment.
method: Applied abliteration (low-rank weight edit projecting out the refusal direction in the residual stream) to Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct models (3B, 7B, 14B) and evaluated on safe code samples from PromSec and SafeCoder.
result: Abliteration reduced refusal to near-zero while maintaining syntactic validity >93%; injection success rates scaled with model size (88-97% for 14B, 25-48% for 3B), separating willingness from capability.
conclusion: Abliteration effectively removes refusal in code LLMs for vulnerability injection, but the approach is specific to code generation and safety alignment, with no direct connection to the user's research areas.

title: Rh+: Row-Hit-Optimized Scheduling For PIM-based Llm Inference
authors: Yongchan Jung, Shafayat Mowla Anik, Byeong Kil Lee, Jeeho Ryoo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model inference on processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures promises to break the memory wall by performing multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations directly within HBM3 DRAM banks. Prior work identifies the power constraint timing parameter nCCDAB as the primary performance bottleneck and optimizes scheduling accordingly. We demonstrate that for GEMV operations that dominate autoregressive decoding, the DRAM row cycle time (nRC) is 10 to 11 times larger than nCCDAB. Consequently, nCCDAB is entirely masked, rendering prior nCCDAB-focused optimizations ineffective for these workloads. The root cause is inherited host-centric address interleaving, which forces every all-bank MAC command into a different DRAM row. We propose RH+ scheduling, a simple stride change that keeps 32 consecutive MAC operations within the same row. Cycle-accurate simulation across four LLM workloads shows that RH+ delivers 8-12x speedup, over 74% energy reduction, and up to 52x EDP improvement.
tldr: This paper proposes a row-hit-optimized scheduling scheme for processing-in-memory architectures to accelerate LLM inference by reducing DRAM row cycle time overhead.
motivation: Prior PIM scheduling optimizations focused on the nCCDAB timing parameter, but for GEMV operations in LLM decoding, the row cycle time nRC is the dominant bottleneck, making previous approaches ineffective.
method: The authors identify that host-centric address interleaving causes all-bank MAC commands to hit different DRAM rows, incurring high nRC latency. They propose RH+ scheduling, a simple stride change that keeps 32 consecutive MAC operations within the same row.
result: Cycle-accurate simulation across four LLM workloads shows 8-12x speedup, over 74% energy reduction, and up to 52x EDP improvement compared to prior scheduling.
conclusion: RH+ effectively addresses the nRC bottleneck for PIM-based LLM inference, offering significant performance and energy gains, and suggests that row-level locality is critical for such workloads.

title: Explainable AI-Driven Cyber Risk Analytics And Model Reliability Assessment For Intelligent Governance Of U.s. Critical Infrastructure: An XGBoost And SHAP-Based Intrusion Detection Framework
authors: B. M. Taslimul Haque, Md. Arifur Rahman, Md. Serajul Kabir Chowdhury Rubel, Md. Iqbal Hossan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing penetrations of the critical infrastructure sector in the United States with intelligent digital technologies have greatly increased exposure to advanced cyber adversaries and operational vulnerabilities. AI-powered governance and automated decision-making systems are becoming a key part of the operation of critical infrastructure systems, including energy, healthcare, transportation, financial services, and communication infrastructure, in order to improve efficiency and strategic management. The growing cyber threat environment, such as Distributed Denial of Service (DDos) attacks, botnets, ransomware, and Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) pose significant challenges to infrastructure resilience, cyber security reliability, and governance trustworthiness. In a changing attack landscape and dynamic network environment, traditional cybersecurity mechanisms can often fall short of meeting the evolving needs and protecting critical systems. This study will develop a resilient cyber risk analytics and model reliability assessment framework to support intelligent governance and decision support for cyber risk exposure in the U.S. critical infrastructure environment. This study is based on the CICIDS2017 dataset for the development and testing of intrusion detection system models and cyber risk prediction models based on machine learning. Various classifiers like XGBoost, Random Forest, and Decision Tree are used to detect malicious activities on the network and determine the level of cyber risk. Furthermore, the Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques are integrated to enhance transparency, interpretability, and trust in cybersecurity decision-making processes. The proposed framework presents the reliability and resilience of the model by having various performance measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC-AUC, and false positive rate.
tldr: This paper applies XGBoost and SHAP for intrusion detection in U.S. critical infrastructure, focusing on cyber risk analytics and model reliability.
motivation: To address the growing cyber threats to critical infrastructure and the limitations of traditional cybersecurity mechanisms.
method: Uses the CICIDS2017 dataset and compares classifiers like XGBoost, Random Forest, and Decision Tree, integrating XAI (SHAP) for interpretability.
result: The proposed framework achieves high performance metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC) and provides explainable predictions.
conclusion: The framework enhances trust and transparency in AI-driven cybersecurity governance, but further validation on real-world data is needed.

title: An Improved Cnn-lstm Based Intrusion Detection System For IoT Networks
authors: Mohammad Tariq Ikhlas, Pohanyar Khowaja Khil, Malik Muhammad Mueed Aslam, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of IoT devices, security concerns have dramatically escalated and intrusion detection systems have become critical for protecting networked environments. This paper presents an improved CNN-LSTM based intrusion detection model that combines multi-class classification, dataset integration, and temporal feature learning to enhance detection performance in IoT networks. Using network traffic data, the proposed approach is evaluated on intrusion detection tasks and achieves an accuracy of approximately 97%. Experimental results demonstrate that the model effectively detects multiple attack categories while maintaining stable training and validation performance. The integration of convolutional and recurrent neural network components enables the framework to capture both spatial and temporal characteristics of network traffic, improving overall intrusion detection capability in IoT environments.
tldr: This paper proposes a CNN-LSTM based intrusion detection system for IoT networks, achieving 97% accuracy on network traffic data.
motivation: To address security concerns in IoT networks by improving intrusion detection performance.
method: Combines convolutional and recurrent neural network components to capture spatial and temporal features of network traffic.
result: The model achieves approximately 97% accuracy in detecting multiple attack categories with stable training and validation performance.
conclusion: The proposed CNN-LSTM model enhances intrusion detection capability in IoT environments, but the paper lacks novelty and depth in the context of the user's research interests.

title: TinyML-Driven Cybersecurity For Autonomous Spacecraft: Latency-Accuracy Analysis For Sparta Rf And Cyber Threat Detection
authors: van Le, Trevor Tran, Tan Le
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous spacecraft require rapid, lightweight, and reliable onboard detection of cyber-RF threats. Using the SPARTA attack model, we analyze the latency-accuracy trade-offs of TinyML-compatible classical models -- Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP -- for detecting uplink jamming, Fake-NR spoofing, payload manipulation, ground-segment compromise, and unauthorized command injection. We present a physics-informed theoretical analysis of each model's computational complexity, VC dimension, Lipschitz continuity, and latency scaling, supported by empirical measurements on adversarial RF spectrograms generated via BandErasure, FakeNR, and NoiseBurst corruption modes. Results show that Logistic Regression achieves microsecond-level inference with only a 1\% accuracy drop relative to Random Forest, making it an effective TinyML baseline for onboard autonomy. The study also identifies opportunities for advancing spacecraft cybersecurity through richer feature encoders and multi-timescale learning architectures, building on recent progress in edge intelligence and trustworthy AI.
tldr: This paper evaluates TinyML models for cyber-RF threat detection in autonomous spacecraft, focusing on latency-accuracy trade-offs.
motivation: Autonomous spacecraft need lightweight onboard detection of cyber-RF threats, but existing solutions may be too heavy or slow.
method: The authors analyze Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP using physics-informed complexity analysis and empirical tests on adversarial RF spectrograms.
result: Logistic Regression achieves microsecond inference with only 1% accuracy drop compared to Random Forest, making it a suitable TinyML baseline.
conclusion: The study suggests future work on richer feature encoders and multi-timescale learning for spacecraft cybersecurity.

title: Towards Worst-case Hardness For Low-Noise Lpn
authors: Divesh Aggarwal, Rishav Gupta, Hai Hoang Nguyen, Kel Zin Tan, Prashant Nalini Vasudevan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hardness of the Learning Parity with Noise (LPN) problem is a foundational assumption in cryptography, forming the basis of constructions ranging from symmetric-key primitives to public-key encryption and beyond. A central open question is whether the average-case hardness of LPN can be based on worst-case complexity assumptions, as has been achieved for the analogous Learning With Errors (LWE) problem. Existing worst-case-to-average-case reductions for LPN [BLVW19, YZ21] rely on statistical smoothing of linear codes, which inherently limits the resulting average-case hardness to noise rates as large as [MATH], which is insufficient for public-key applications. We explore a new approach towards obtaining such reductions: rather than requiring that random sparse combinations of the rows of the generator matrix of a code be statistically close to uniform, we only require that they be computationally indistinguishable from uniform. This leads to a clean win-win structure: we show that any efficient LPN solver can be transformed into a pair of efficient algorithms [MATH] such that for every matrix [MATH] of appropriate dimensions over [MATH], either [MATH] decodes the code generated by [MATH] from random noise, or [MATH] distinguishes random noisy codewords of the dual of this code from uniform. By instantiating this reduction with appropriate parameters, we obtain the average-case hardness of LPN with inverse-polynomial noise rate [MATH] for any constant [MATH], assuming the worst-case simultaneous hardness of decoding a code from random noise and distinguishing random noisy codewords of its dual from uniform. In particular, setting [MATH], our reduction yields LPN hardness in the parameter regime required for Alekhnovich's construction of public-key encryption [Ale03], a regime that was previously inaccessible via worst-case reductions.
tldr: This paper proposes a new approach to prove worst-case hardness for the Learning Parity with Noise (LPN) problem, aiming to enable public-key encryption from worst-case assumptions.
motivation: Existing worst-case-to-average-case reductions for LPN only work for high noise rates, insufficient for public-key applications. The authors aim to achieve reductions for low-noise LPN.
method: Instead of requiring statistical smoothing of linear codes, they only require computational indistinguishability, leading to a win-win reduction that transforms any LPN solver into either a decoder or a distinguisher.
result: They obtain average-case hardness of LPN with inverse-polynomial noise rate under worst-case hardness of decoding and distinguishing dual codewords, covering the regime needed for Alekhnovich's public-key encryption.
conclusion: This work provides a new path to worst-case hardness for low-noise LPN, potentially enabling public-key cryptography based on LPN from worst-case assumptions.

title: Exploring Cooperation Mechanisms Via Reinforcement Learning In Network Common-pool Resource Games
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustaining cooperation in resource-constrained populations requires allocation mechanisms that balance individual incentives, resource sustainability, and distributional fairness. This paper proposes a network common-pool resource game in which individuals are embedded in complex networks, participate in multiple overlapping local resource pools, and face endogenous resource constraints during strategy evolution. Within this framework, we first examine two representative allocation mechanisms, equal allocation and proportional allocation. The results show that equal allocation produces fair but inefficient outcomes by weakening contribution incentives, whereas proportional allocation can temporarily promote cooperation but amplifies accumulated advantages and leads to severe inequality. To overcome these limitations, we develop a graph neural network-based reinforcement learning framework in which a learned social planner allocates local pool resources without directly controlling individual strategies. Simulation results under four representative network topologies show that the learned planner sustains higher cooperation levels and average accumulated resources, and reduces inequality compared with the baselines. Furthermore, we interpret the learned policy and distill it into two simpler mechanisms: a resource-dependent mixture mechanism for regular networks and a degree-conditioned mixture mechanism for heterogeneous networks. These mechanisms reveal that effective allocation should adapt to both local resource states and structural positions, providing an interpretable route from reinforcement learning policy search to mechanism design in networked resource-sharing systems.
tldr: This paper uses reinforcement learning to design allocation mechanisms in network common-pool resource games, focusing on cooperation and fairness.
motivation: To overcome limitations of equal and proportional allocation mechanisms in sustaining cooperation and reducing inequality in networked resource-sharing systems.
method: A graph neural network-based reinforcement learning framework where a learned social planner allocates local pool resources without controlling individual strategies.
result: The learned planner sustains higher cooperation levels, average accumulated resources, and reduces inequality compared to baselines across four network topologies.
conclusion: Effective allocation should adapt to local resource states and structural positions, providing an interpretable route from RL policy search to mechanism design.

title: Metric Facility Assignment With Partial Information
authors: Vasilis Gkatzelis, Hasti Karimi, Emma Rewinski, Maziar Shamsipour, Alexandros A. Voudouris
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an assignment problem where a set of agents and a set of facilities lie on a line metric. The goal is to compute an assignment of agents to facilities to approximately minimize the social cost (the total distance of agents from their assigned facilities) given only partial information regarding the metric. Unlike previous work which focused solely on algorithms with access to the ordinal preferences of the agents over the facilities (ORD), we also consider the value of information regarding approval preferences (APP), and inter-facility distances (DIST). For different combinations of these three information types, we establish tight bounds on the distortion of deterministic algorithms, showing that it is possible to improve over the optimal bound of [MATH] that can be achieved using only ORD information. Among other results, we show a tight bound of [MATH] for APP+DIST which holds even for general metrics, and a tight bound of [MATH] for ORD+APP+DIST.
tldr: This paper studies metric facility assignment with partial information, focusing on distortion bounds for different information types, which is unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: To understand how different types of partial information (ordinal, approval, distances) affect the quality of facility assignment algorithms.
method: The authors analyze deterministic algorithms for assignment on a line metric, proving tight distortion bounds for combinations of ORD, APP, and DIST information.
result: Tight bounds are established, e.g., APP+DIST achieves distortion 3 even for general metrics, and ORD+APP+DIST achieves distortion 2.
conclusion: The work provides a complete picture of achievable distortion under various information constraints, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Regret Minimization In Single-Dimensional Contract-Design With Binary Actions
authors: Riccardo Poiani, Martino Bernasconi, Andrea Celli
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study principal-agent problems in which a principal commits to an outcome-dependent payment scheme (i.e., a contract) in order to induce an agent to take a costly action leading to a favorable outcome. We consider the online extension of the classical (one-shot) principal-agent problem, in which the principal repeatedly interacts with agents by proposing contracts over multiple rounds. The principal has no information about the agents and, crucially, does not observe their actions. As a result, the principal must learn an optimal contract using only the realized outcomes observed at each round. We focus on the setting with binary actions and single-dimensional agent types, where the agent's private type represents their cost per unit-of-effort. For adversarial-type sequences, we provide tight [MATH] regret guarantees. Remarkably, this rate is completely independent of the number of outcomes [MATH]. The upper bound is based on two key components: 1) a reduction to a one-dimensional threshold optimization problem and 2) a non-uniform discretization to handle the non-Lipschitz nature of the problem. Moreover, in the case of a single (fixed) hidden type, we show that it is possible to improve the rates and provide a tight [MATH] regret bound. Our algorithm is based on an explore-then-commit strategy where we first approximately learn the hidden type via a stochastic binary search, and then we commit to a ``robustified'' near-optimal contract.
tldr: This paper studies online contract design with binary actions and single-dimensional agent types, providing regret bounds for learning optimal contracts without observing agent actions.
motivation: To extend classical principal-agent problems to an online setting where the principal must learn an optimal contract from observed outcomes without knowing agent types or actions.
method: Reduces the problem to one-dimensional threshold optimization and uses non-uniform discretization to handle non-Lipschitzness; for fixed hidden type, uses explore-then-commit with stochastic binary search.
result: Achieves tight regret bounds independent of the number of outcomes for adversarial-type sequences, and improved bounds for a single fixed hidden type.
conclusion: Provides foundational regret guarantees for online contract design, with potential extensions to more complex settings.

title: Decoupling Adhesion From Jamming In Phase Transitions Drives Tissue Organization
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how adhesion and cell density control phase transitions in tissue organization, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how mechanical properties like adhesion and jamming regulate tissue material state and developmental programs.
method: Combined in silico modeling and in vivo experiments to independently tune cell density and adhesion.
result: Adhesion dictates the tissue material state; adhesion-driven solidification in unjammed pluripotent tissues drives epithelial organization.
conclusion: Phase transitions direct developmental programs, highlighting the role of adhesion in tissue organization.

title: Universal Deformations And Universal Residual Stresses In Incompressible Isotropic Cauchy Elasticity
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study universal deformations in incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids with residual stress, without assuming any specific origin for the residual stress. Starting from the constitutive representation of the Cauchy stress as an isotropic tensor-valued function of strain and residual stress, we derive the universality constraints for residually-stressed incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids. We show that for the six known families of universal deformations the set of universal deformations is identical to that of incompressible isotropic elasticity in the absence of residual stress. We also show that residual stress does not enlarge the space of universal deformations. We then determine the universal residual stress fields corresponding to the six known families of universal deformations. Assuming that the residual stress field has the same symmetry as the corresponding universal deformation, the universality constraints reduce to systems of ordinary differential equations that can be solved explicitly. The resulting universal residual stress fields are characterized and discussed for each family.
tldr: This paper studies universal deformations and residual stresses in incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how residual stress affects universal deformations in nonlinear elasticity, without assuming a specific origin for the stress.
method: Derives universality constraints from constitutive representation of Cauchy stress as isotropic function of strain and residual stress, then solves ODEs for symmetric residual stress fields.
result: The set of universal deformations is identical to that without residual stress; residual stress does not enlarge the space. Universal residual stress fields are characterized for six deformation families.
conclusion: Provides a framework for analyzing residual stress in elastic solids, but no implications for quantum systems or information thermodynamics.

title: Entropy-Compatible Barrier Schemes For Diffusive Fene Flows
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: FENE-type conformation-tensor models impose a finite-extensibility constraint that is absent from Oldroyd--B flow: the conformation tensor must satisfy [MATH] and [MATH]. Positive definiteness alone is therefore insufficient, since a numerical state can remain positive while crossing the singular trace barrier. Even a trace-preserving logarithmic parametrization is not enough by itself: high-order reconstruction can remain inside the finite-extensibility domain while injecting artificial FENE entropy. We develop and analyze a barrier-preserving entropy-compatible discretization for FENE-P type flows with polymer center-of-mass molecular diffusion and for trace-singular FENE-family closures with the same entropy structure. The method combines a trace-barrier free energy, a finite-extensibility logarithmic parametrization, a least-damping entropy-compatible barrier-log reconstruction, molecular diffusion paired with the barrier entropy variable, compatible quadrature for polymeric work, and a scaled FENE stress variable for the small-Weissenberg limit. For admissible discrete states we prove finite-extensibility preservation at entropy quadrature points, existence and bisection computability of the maximal entropy-admissible reconstruction parameter, a fully discrete free-energy inequality with relaxation and molecular-diffusion barrier dissipation, a quantitative AP stress closure, and a fixed-discretization Newtonian limit. A conditional relative-entropy estimate is derived on compact subsets of the finite-extensibility domain. Numerical diagnostics verify barrier preservation, entropy-compatible reconstruction, energy decay, AP closure, coupled velocity--pressure--stress accuracy, and high-Weissenberg robustness near the trace constraint.
tldr: This paper develops entropy-compatible numerical schemes for FENE-type polymer flow models, focusing on preserving finite-extensibility constraints and thermodynamic consistency.
motivation: Standard numerical methods for FENE-type flows can violate the finite-extensibility constraint or introduce artificial entropy, leading to unphysical results. The research aims to develop a discretization that preserves the trace barrier and entropy structure.
method: The method combines a trace-barrier free energy, a logarithmic parametrization, a barrier-preserving reconstruction, compatible quadrature, and a scaled stress variable. It includes proofs of finite-extensibility preservation, free-energy inequality, and asymptotic-preserving properties.
result: Key results include finite-extensibility preservation at quadrature points, a fully discrete free-energy inequality with barrier dissipation, a quantitative AP stress closure, and a conditional relative-entropy estimate. Numerical tests confirm barrier preservation, entropy compatibility, and robustness near the trace constraint.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a thermodynamically consistent numerical framework for FENE-type flows, with implications for simulating polymer dynamics under high Weissenberg numbers. Future work may extend to more complex closures or coupled physics.

title: Introduction To Measure And Integration Theory
authors: Hugo Guadalupe Reyna-Casta\~neda, Mar\'ia de Los \'angeles Sandoval-Romero, Luis Antonio Cede\~no-P\'erez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These notes provide a rigorous and accessible introduction to measure and integration theory, with emphasis on the conceptual transition from the Riemann integral to the Lebesgue integral and the role played by limiting processes in modern analysis. The manuscript develops the basic theory of measurable sets, measurable functions, measures on [MATH]-algebras, Lebesgue integration, convergence theorems, and [MATH] spaces. Particular attention is devoted to the interaction between integration and convergence, as well as to the limitations of the Riemann integral that motivate the development of measure theory. The exposition seeks to balance mathematical rigor with pedagogical clarity through detailed proofs, examples, exercises, and supplementary projects. These notes are intended primarily for undergraduate students in mathematics and related areas encountering measure theory for the first time, although they may also serve as a reference for introductory graduate courses in analysis.
tldr: These notes provide an introduction to measure and integration theory, covering Lebesgue integration and convergence theorems.
motivation: To offer a rigorous yet accessible introduction to measure theory for undergraduate students, bridging the gap from Riemann to Lebesgue integration.
method: Pedagogical exposition with detailed proofs, examples, exercises, and supplementary projects.
result: Development of basic theory of measurable sets, functions, measures, Lebesgue integration, convergence theorems, and L^p spaces.
conclusion: Serves as a textbook for students new to measure theory, with no direct implications for the user's research areas.

title: Counting Votes With Multisets
authors: Bart Jacobs, Michael Johnson, Richard Buckland
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A multiset is a 'set' in which elements may occur multiple times. These structures are ideal for expressing the outcome of an election, for instance of the form 60 'yes' and 40 'no'. Moreover, multisets are a useful datatype in vote counting algorithms. This will be illustrated in three different forms of vote counting, known as: 'instant-runoff', 'De Borda', and 'single transferrable vote'. The relevant abstract properties of multisets are: (1) they form a (free) commutative monoid, and (2) they form a functor, and (3) also a monad. This paper illustrates how such categorical properties can be put to good use in deriving and expressing election outcomes. The emphasis is not on the (elementary) category theory involved, but on its application in voting systems.
tldr: This paper uses categorical properties of multisets to model and derive vote counting algorithms for instant-runoff, De Borda, and single transferable vote systems.
motivation: To demonstrate how abstract mathematical structures (multisets as commutative monoids, functors, and monads) can be applied to practical problems in election theory.
method: The authors formalize multisets categorically and show how their algebraic properties simplify the expression and derivation of vote counting procedures.
result: They illustrate that multisets provide a natural and elegant framework for describing and computing election outcomes in three different voting systems.
conclusion: The work highlights the utility of category theory in applied domains like voting, but does not address quantum or thermodynamic aspects relevant to the user's interests.

title: The {\alpha} -Discounting ({\alpha}-DMCDM) As An Extension Of Ahp, Topsis, Vikor, Promethee, And Weighted Sum
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and other classic Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) techniques excel when decision makers can provide consistent pair wise judgments. Real world problems, however, often involve inconsistent, n-wise, or non-linear preference structures that render traditional methods inadequate. The {\alpha}-Discounting MCDM ({\alpha}-D MCDM) extends AHP by embedding a global discounting parameter {\alpha} that transforms an inconsistent system of preference equations into a solvable algebraic system.
tldr: This paper proposes an extension of multi-criteria decision making methods using a discounting parameter to handle inconsistent preferences.
motivation: Classic MCDM methods like AHP require consistent pairwise comparisons, which are often unrealistic in real-world problems.
method: The α-Discounting MCDM embeds a global discounting parameter α to transform inconsistent preference equations into a solvable algebraic system.
result: The method extends AHP, TOPSIS, VIKOR, PROMETHEE, and weighted sum to handle inconsistent, n-wise, or non-linear preferences.
conclusion: The approach broadens the applicability of MCDM methods but is not directly related to quantum computing or information thermodynamics.

title: N-ary Quasi-arithmetic Means And Families Without Regularity
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical theorems of Kolmogorov--Nagumo--de Finetti and of Aczel--Maksa characterize quasi-arithmetic means from two complementary directions: the former for compatible families of means satisfying the replacement axiom, and the latter for bisymmetric means of fixed arity. We refine both representation results by showing that the required continuity follows automatically. Our main result states that every reflexive, symmetric, bisymmetric and partially strictly increasing [MATH]-variable operation on a real interval is continuous and hence quasi-arithmetic. The proof is based on a recursive construction on [MATH]-adic rationals given by bisymmetry, and a dense-domain continuity argument. The same method also yields the regularity-free Kolmogorov--Nagumo--de Finetti theorem for compatible families of strictly increasing symmetric means.
tldr: The paper proves that continuity in quasi-arithmetic mean characterizations follows from other axioms, removing the need for a separate regularity assumption.
motivation: To refine classical theorems (Kolmogorov-Nagumo-de Finetti and Aczel-Maksa) by showing that continuity is automatically implied by the other axioms, thus simplifying the characterization of quasi-arithmetic means.
method: The authors use a recursive construction on N-adic rationals based on bisymmetry and a dense-domain continuity argument to prove that reflexive, symmetric, bisymmetric, and partially strictly increasing operations are continuous and hence quasi-arithmetic.
result: Every reflexive, symmetric, bisymmetric, and partially strictly increasing operation on a real interval is continuous and therefore quasi-arithmetic. The same method yields a regularity-free version of the Kolmogorov-Nagumo-de Finetti theorem.
conclusion: The results strengthen the foundations of mean theory by eliminating the need for explicit continuity assumptions, which may have implications for aggregation theory and functional equations.

title: Some Properties Of Besov-Morrey Type Spaces
authors: A. Ussentay, K. Sadykova, N. Tleukhanova
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers Sobolev-Morrey and Besov-Morrey spaces. For Morrey spaces, multipliers are studied, and a theorem on multipliers from M_p^lambda(T) to M_p^lambda(T) is obtained for 1 < p < infinity and 0 <= lambda < 1/p. Based on this result, embeddings between Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-type spaces are established, namely B_1^alpha(M_p^lambda) embedded into W^alpha(M_p^lambda) embedded into B_infinity^alpha(M_p^lambda) for 0 < p <= infinity, 0 <= lambda <= 1/p, and alpha in R. In addition, an interpolation theorem for Besov-Morrey spaces is proved.
tldr: This paper studies embeddings and interpolation theorems for Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-Morrey function spaces.
motivation: To extend classical function space theory to Morrey-type spaces, which are useful in PDEs and harmonic analysis.
method: The authors analyze multipliers on Morrey spaces and use them to prove embedding results between Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-Morrey spaces, and also prove an interpolation theorem.
result: They obtain embeddings B_1^α(M_p^λ) ⊂ W^α(M_p^λ) ⊂ B_∞^α(M_p^λ) and an interpolation result for Besov-Morrey spaces.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of function spaces, but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On Parallel And Batch-Cutting Strategies For Norm-Minimization-Based Convex Vector Optimization
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop parallel and batch-cutting variants of the norm-minimization-based outer approximation algorithm for convex vector optimization. The standard algorithm solves [MATH] independent subproblems at each iteration~[MATH] to evaluate all vertices of the current polyhedral approximation, but processes only the single best cut. We propose two improvements. First, we parallelize the across [MATH] workers, reducing per-iteration wall-clock time. Second, we introduce a batch-cutting strategy that adds up to [MATH] supporting halfspaces per iteration, using information from all solved subproblems rather than discarding it. We prove that the batch-cutting variant inherits the convergence rate [MATH] of the standard algorithm, where [MATH] is the number of outer iterations and [MATH] is the number of objectives. Computational experiments on eight test problems with [MATH] show that parallelism on 8 cores , and batch cutting consistently reduces the iteration count by 62--80\%. However, the wall-clock benefit of batch cutting is problem-dependent: the additional cuts per iteration accelerate vertex count growth, so batch cutting is most effective when per-vertex subproblem cost dominates.
tldr: This paper proposes parallel and batch-cutting strategies for a norm-minimization-based convex vector optimization algorithm, improving computational efficiency.
motivation: The standard algorithm solves many independent subproblems per iteration but only uses one cut, wasting computation. The authors aim to reduce wall-clock time and iteration count.
method: Parallelization distributes subproblem solving across workers, and batch-cutting adds multiple supporting halfspaces per iteration using all subproblem solutions.
result: Parallelism on 8 cores and batch cutting reduce iteration count by 62-80%, but wall-clock benefit of batch cutting depends on per-vertex subproblem cost.
conclusion: The batch-cutting variant retains convergence rate and can be more efficient when subproblem cost dominates, but effectiveness varies by problem.

title: Derivations Of Rational Vertex Operator Algebras Are Inner
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that every derivation of a simple and rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type is an inner derivation.
tldr: This paper proves that all derivations of simple rational vertex operator algebras of CFT type are inner derivations.
motivation: To understand the structure of derivations in vertex operator algebras, which is important for the algebraic theory of conformal field theory.
method: The paper uses algebraic methods within the theory of vertex operator algebras, likely involving cohomology or representation theory.
result: Every derivation of a simple rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type is inner.
conclusion: This result clarifies the derivation algebra of such vertex operator algebras, with implications for their automorphism groups and deformation theory.

title: Combining Diffuse And Sharp Interface Methods In Shape Optimisation
authors: Philip J. Herbert, Michael Hinze, Christian Kahle
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a concept for the numerical treatment of shape optimization problems based on the combination of phase field and sharp interface methods. On the one hand, phase field methods are very well suited to numerically determine the shape, size and topology of a sought domain, but on the other hand they have problems to sharpen out domains where they e.g. should develop corners. However, this is the strength of a sharp-interface approach developed in our group, which provides shape updates in the Lipschitz topology. This leads to a two-stage process that first determines an optimized shape using the phase field method. The resulting domain is the starting solution for the sharp interface shape optimization method. Both methods are discretized with the finite element method. The starting mesh for the sharp method is constructed from the finite element mesh of the optimal phase field solution using its properly post processed zero-level set. We describe this construction process in detail and investigate the performance of our method on a selection of test problems from the literature and from applications.
tldr: This paper combines phase field and sharp interface methods for shape optimization, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To overcome limitations of phase field methods in resolving sharp features like corners by integrating a sharp interface approach.
method: A two-stage process: first, phase field optimization to find an approximate shape; second, sharp interface refinement using Lipschitz topology updates, both discretized with finite elements.
result: The combined method successfully produces optimized shapes with sharp corners, demonstrated on test problems.
conclusion: The hybrid approach improves shape optimization accuracy, but the paper is purely in computational mathematics and engineering.

title: Domain-Conditioned Safety In Frontier Computer-Using Agents: A 793-Episode Browser Benchmark, A Coding-Domain Cross-Reference, And A Reproducibility Audit Of Recent Red-Teaming
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent computer-using-agent (CUA) red-teaming papers report prompt-injection attack success rates (ASR) of 42-98%, but these headline numbers cluster on retired models and on the most-vulnerable model in each paper's panel. We ask whether those techniques, reproduced as hand-crafted templates, still work against current frontier CUAs. We release CUA-HandCrafted, a public benchmark of 793 episodes spanning 24 multi-step web tasks, 56 attack templates, 8 attack families, and 4 system-prompt configurations. Against Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.4 we measure 0/140 multi-step attack success (Clopper-Pearson 95% upper bound 2.60%); a prompt ablation shows this resistance lives in the model weights. Yet it does not generalize: on a sister coding-agent benchmark (SkillBench), the same weights fall to hand-crafted skill-injection at up to 100%. We argue that the literature's high ASR is largely attributable to RL-optimized injection text rather than the attack categories, and that frontier safety hardening is domain-conditioned, specific to the heavily-targeted browser surface. Reporting techniques without releasing the optimized strings, or extrapolating browser-domain safety to other CUA modalities, makes published ASR numbers unreproducible.
tldr: This paper evaluates prompt-injection attack success rates on frontier computer-using agents, finding near-zero success on browser tasks but high vulnerability on coding tasks, highlighting domain-conditioned safety.
motivation: Recent red-teaming papers report high attack success rates on older models, but reproducibility and generalization to current models are unclear.
method: The authors create a benchmark of 793 episodes with hand-crafted attack templates and test against Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.4, including ablation studies and a coding-agent benchmark.
result: Zero multi-step attack success on browser tasks (95% upper bound 2.60%), but up to 100% success on coding tasks; resistance is in model weights and domain-specific.
conclusion: Published high ASR numbers are not reproducible with hand-crafted templates on current models, and safety hardening is domain-conditioned, not generalizable across modalities.

title: Bitcoin After Block Rewards
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bitcoin's block reward is scheduled to decline to zero, raising concerns about whether the network can remain secure once miners rely solely on transaction fees. This paper seeks to identify the conditions under which large-scale and persistent deviation from honest mining can arise. We analyze and compare the payoffs of honest and deviating miners in a sequential decision model, and identify a deviation threshold [MATH] at which honest mining ceases to be privately optimal. Around the 2024 Bitcoin halving, we show that current mining behavior does not exhibit large-scale or structural deviation. However, when the block reward is removed, the [MATH] criterion implies that deviation can arise even with a very small fraction of transaction fees. Finally, we evaluate three protocol-level mechanisms: Base Fee, Fee Floor, and an adaptive maximum block size rule, and show that their combination raises the deviation threshold and mitigates incentive breakdown in a fee-only regime. These results provide a practical benchmark for assessing Bitcoin's security as block rewards disappear.
tldr: This paper analyzes Bitcoin's security after block rewards end, focusing on miner incentives and protocol mechanisms to prevent deviation.
motivation: Bitcoin's block reward will eventually disappear, raising concerns about network security when miners rely solely on transaction fees.
method: The authors use a sequential decision model to compare payoffs of honest and deviating miners, and evaluate three protocol-level mechanisms (Base Fee, Fee Floor, adaptive max block size).
result: Current mining behavior shows no large-scale deviation, but after block rewards end, deviation can arise even with small transaction fees; the proposed mechanisms raise the deviation threshold.
conclusion: The combination of fee mechanisms can mitigate incentive breakdown, providing a benchmark for Bitcoin's security in a fee-only regime.

title: Dimensionality Reduction For Cyberattack Classification: A Comparative Evaluation Of Pca And Linear Predictive Coding
authors: Nelly Elsayed, Zag Elsayed, Navid Asadizanjani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional feature representations are widely used in machine learning-based cyberattack detection systems. However, they increase computational complexity and may hinder deployment in resource-constrained environments. In this paper, we investigate feature compression techniques for cyberattack classification by comparing two dimensionality reduction approaches: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Linear Predictive Coding (LPC). Compressed feature representations with varying dimensionalities are generated and evaluated across several classification models. Experimental analysis demonstrates that PCA preserves classification performance even under aggressive compression. On the other hand, LPC provides competitive predictive representations with slightly larger performance degradation. The results show that substantial reductions in feature dimensionality can be achieved with minimal impact on classification accuracy, highlighting the potential of lightweight feature compression for efficient cybersecurity analytics.
tldr: This paper compares PCA and LPC for dimensionality reduction in cyberattack classification, showing that PCA preserves accuracy under aggressive compression.
motivation: High-dimensional feature representations in cyberattack detection increase computational complexity, hindering deployment in resource-constrained environments.
method: The authors generate compressed feature representations using PCA and LPC at varying dimensionalities and evaluate them across several classification models.
result: PCA preserves classification performance even under aggressive compression, while LPC shows slightly larger performance degradation.
conclusion: Substantial reductions in feature dimensionality can be achieved with minimal impact on classification accuracy, highlighting the potential of lightweight feature compression for efficient cybersecurity analytics.

title: Cognitive Threat Intelligence And Explainable Federated Security Analytics For Distributed Infrastructure Systems
authors: Md. Arifur Rahman, B. M. Taslimul Haque, Md. Iqbal Hossan, Md. Serajul Kabir Chowdhury Rubel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing adoption of distributed infrastructure systems, cloud computing, Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, and edge-based architectures has significantly expanded the cybersecurity attack surface and introduced increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. Conventional centralized intrusion detection approaches often face challenges related to scalability, data privacy, communication overhead, and limited transparency in artificial intelligence-driven decision-making processes. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Cognitive Threat Intelligence and Explainable Federated Security Analytics framework for distributed infrastructure systems. The proposed framework integrates Federated Learning (FL), Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), and cognitive cybersecurity analytics to enable collaborative and privacy-preserving cyber threat detection across distributed network environments. Instead of transmitting sensitive raw network traffic data to centralized servers, local security models are independently trained at distributed nodes, where only encrypted model parameters and updates are shared through a federated aggregation mechanism. This decentralized learning architecture improves privacy protection while reducing communication dependency and centralized security risks. To enhance intelligent threat analysis, the framework incorporates machine learning and deep learning algorithms including Random Forest, XGBoost, Autoencoder.
tldr: This paper proposes a federated learning framework with explainable AI for cybersecurity threat detection in distributed systems, but it is unrelated to quantum computing, information thermodynamics, or quantum communication.
motivation: To address scalability, privacy, and transparency issues in centralized intrusion detection for distributed infrastructure systems.
method: Integrates Federated Learning, Explainable AI, and cognitive analytics; local models are trained on distributed nodes and only encrypted parameters are shared.
result: The framework enables privacy-preserving collaborative threat detection, but no experimental results or performance metrics are provided in the abstract.
conclusion: The approach may improve security and transparency, but lacks novelty in the context of the user's research interests.

title: An Embarrassingly Simple Detector For Model Extraction Attacks In Large Language Model Api Traffic
authors: Shuze Liu, Qianwen Guo, Yushun Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed through hosted APIs, making model extraction a practical threat to model ownership and service security. However, individual extraction queries often resemble benign requests, and existing evaluations often focus on single-query anomaly scoring or pure benign-versus-attacker user settings. We formulate model extraction monitoring as benign-calibrated traffic-window distribution testing and show that an embarrassingly simple detector is effective: embed incoming queries into a semantic space and test whether their aggregate distribution deviates from historical benign traffic. We instantiate the detector with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), using only benign-vs-benign comparisons to set the decision threshold. We evaluate on fourteen attacker-normal query pairs from four extraction scenarios and compare with adapted PRADA, SEAT, CAP, DATE, and marginal Mahalanobis baselines. Across three random seeds, MMD achieves 0.3% benign FPR, 100.0% pure-attacker TPR, 90.5% average TPR over attacker fractions, and 95.1% balanced accuracy. These results show that benign-calibrated distribution testing is a strong empirical baseline for model extraction detection in both user-level and mixed multi-user LLM API traffic. Code is released at: [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes a simple detector for model extraction attacks on LLM APIs using distribution testing with MMD.
motivation: Model extraction attacks threaten LLM ownership, but existing detection methods are complex or focus on single queries.
method: The detector embeds queries into a semantic space and uses maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) to compare the distribution of incoming traffic against historical benign traffic, with thresholds set using benign-vs-benign comparisons.
result: The MMD detector achieves 0.3% benign FPR, 100% pure-attacker TPR, 90.5% average TPR, and 95.1% balanced accuracy across multiple attack scenarios.
conclusion: Benign-calibrated distribution testing is a strong baseline for model extraction detection in LLM API traffic, with potential for further improvement.

title: SentinelRAG: Synthetic Sentinel Knowledge For Rag Database Copyright Protection
authors: Tsun On Kwok, Xi Yang, Ki Sen Hung, Chang Liu, Yangqiu Song
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protecting proprietary RAG databases from unauthorized redistribution is challenging: existing watermarking methods either inject fabricated relations between real entities, polluting the knowledge base with misinformation, or embed fragile lexical patterns that adversarial paraphrasing easily removes. We propose SentinelRAG, a watermarking framework that embeds style-consistent but fictitious knowledge entries into the RAG database. Our key insight is that synthetic knowledge describing fictitious entities is unlikely to be retrieved by legitimate queries, yet can be reliably triggered through targeted probes known only to the data owner. Experiments on four datasets ranging from 2.9k to 8.8M documents demonstrate that SentinelRAG achieves statistically significant detection [MATH] across all tested configurations at only a 0.1% injection rate. Compared to the state-of-the-art, our method significantly reduces the false detection rate while maintaining negligible interference with legitimate user queries.
tldr: SentinelRAG embeds fictitious knowledge entries into RAG databases for copyright protection, with minimal impact on legitimate queries.
motivation: Protecting proprietary RAG databases from unauthorized redistribution is challenging; existing watermarking methods either pollute the knowledge base with misinformation or are easily removed by paraphrasing.
method: The framework injects style-consistent but fictitious knowledge entries describing nonexistent entities, which are unlikely to be retrieved by legitimate queries but can be triggered by targeted probes known only to the data owner.
result: Experiments on four datasets (2.9k to 8.8M documents) show statistically significant detection at only 0.1% injection rate, with reduced false detection rate and negligible interference with legitimate queries.
conclusion: SentinelRAG offers a robust watermarking method for RAG databases, but its focus on copyright protection is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: GenTI: Benchmarking LLMs For Autonomous Idps Rule Generation For Unseen Attacks
authors: Hassan Jalil Hadi, Rehana Yasmin, Ali Shoker
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rule-based Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDPS) offer precise attack detection as well as mitigation, however their manually crafted, signature-driven rules limit adaptability to emerging and zero-day threats. Additionally, existing public datasets (e.g., CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15) focus on traffic classification and provide little structured information to support automatic rule synthesis or prevention logic. To address this gap, we propose Generative Thread Intelligence (GenTI) an LLM-driven benchmark for automatic generation of IDPS rules targeting unseen attacks. The dataset (GTI) aggregates over 150k detection and prevention rules from Snort, Suricata, Emerging Threats, as well as 50k YARA, each annotated with protocol behavior, payload signatures, contextual relationships, mappings to Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI), along with actionable response types (alert, drop, reject). Moreover, on top of this corpus we design an LLM-based pipeline that transforms analyst prompts and representative payloads into deployable rules via structured prompt engineering, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, as well as a Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) loop for syntactic, semantic, and security validation. The generated rules are executed in real time on (Snort/Suricata) and evaluated by syntax accuracy, semantic similarity, CTI coverage, security effectiveness as well as unseen attacks detection. Furthermore, our GenTI instantiation achieves a composite rule-quality score of 89.4\%, with 94.8\% CTI coverage, improving unseen attacks detection from 45\% to 87.4\% and reducing the false-positive rate from 8.5\% to 2.3\%. Overall, GenTI establishes the first large-scale benchmark that tightly couples rule-level CTI with LLM-based automation, enabling adaptive, self-evolving IDPS.
tldr: This paper introduces GenTI, a benchmark and LLM-based pipeline for automatically generating IDPS rules to detect unseen attacks.
motivation: Existing rule-based IDPS systems rely on manually crafted signatures, limiting adaptability to zero-day threats, and current datasets lack structured information for automatic rule synthesis.
method: The authors aggregate over 200k detection/prevention rules from Snort, Suricata, Emerging Threats, and YARA, annotated with protocol behavior, payload signatures, and CTI mappings. They design an LLM pipeline using prompt engineering, Chain-of-Thought reasoning, and Chain-of-Verification loops to generate deployable rules, which are evaluated on syntax accuracy, semantic similarity, CTI coverage, and security effectiveness.
result: GenTI achieves a composite rule-quality score of 89.4%, 94.8% CTI coverage, improves unseen attack detection from 45% to 87.4%, and reduces false-positive rate from 8.5% to 2.3%.
conclusion: GenTI establishes a large-scale benchmark coupling rule-level CTI with LLM automation, enabling adaptive, self-evolving IDPS systems.

title: Exploring The Connection Between Coding Habits And Cognitive Styles In Malware Developers
authors: Vasilis Vouvoutsis, Constantinos Patsakis, Fran Casino
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Malware research primarily studies the results, the methods, and the impact. Even from an offensive security perspective, what is examined is the method, not the development strategy of the offender. This study investigates the behavioral signatures and coding patterns embedded in the malware source code. By analyzing a large corpus of leaked malware code and comparing it with carefully selected benign open-source software, we apply static application security testing and compute multiple software metrics. Based on cognitive psychology and criminological theories, our work interprets differences in code structure and quality as behavioral indicators, reflecting distinct motivational structures, risk tolerances, and development strategies of malware authors compared to benign software developers. Our findings reveal that malware code is generally smaller, less documented, and exhibits higher cyclomatic complexity per function, with reduced use of abstraction mechanisms such as classes and closures. Vulnerability analysis further reveals that malware exhibits more issues of the types that benign code typically avoids, suggesting a minimal investment in secure development practices. These patterns imply a development style optimized for expedience, operational secrecy, and evasion rather than long-term maintainability. Nonetheless, the code quality metrics indicate that it does not deviate significantly from benign software enough to be distinctive. By framing code metrics as proxies for behavioral signals and strategic choices, we demonstrate how quantitative software analysis can enrich behavioral cybersecurity research, offering new insights into the practices and priorities of malware developers. Our results pave the way for further research in the behavioral profiling of cyber offenders.
tldr: This paper analyzes coding habits in malware developers using software metrics and cognitive psychology, but is unrelated to quantum computing or information thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand behavioral signatures of malware authors by analyzing source code, bridging cybersecurity and cognitive psychology.
method: Applied static application security testing and computed software metrics on leaked malware code compared to benign open-source software.
result: Malware code is smaller, less documented, has higher cyclomatic complexity, and more security issues, but overall quality differences are not extreme.
conclusion: Quantitative software analysis can enrich behavioral cybersecurity research, but the findings are preliminary and not directly applicable to quantum information science.

title: AttackPathGNN: Cross-function Vulnerability Detection In Smart Contracts Using State Interference Graphs And Conjunction Pooling
authors: Gabriela Dobrita, Simona-Vasilica Oprea, Adela Bara
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing learning-based detectors for Solidity smart-contracts reduce vulnerability detection to syntactic pattern matching within single functions, yet many of the most consequential exploits (The DAO, Cream Finance) exist not in any individual function but in the relationship between functions and in the combination of conditions that made the attack feasible. Thus, we propose AttackPathGNN, a graph neural network (GNN) that reframes detection as reasoning over explicit attack paths. Two architectural choices distinguish it from prior GNN-based detectors: (1)a State Interference Graph that links every pair of functions sharing mutable storage through typed, weighted edges and through directed reentrancy-path edges defined by an explicit five-condition predicate; (2)conjunction pooling, a differentiable AND-aggregator over eight named exploit preconditions whose log-sigmoid form causes the per-function exploit score to collapse whenever any single mitigation (a reentrancy guard, an access-control modifier or SafeMath) is in place. Across five independent training runs, AttackPathGNN attains 92.3+/-0.2% F1 on the SmartBugs Wild held-out test partition (4.3+/-0.3% false-negative rate, 90.8+/-2.5% detection rate on the independently human-labelled SmartBugs Curated benchmark), recovering 6/10 DASP10 categories at 100% on every seed and Reentrancy at 98.7+/-1.8%. Each prediction is emitted with a structured remediation report, turning each verdict into an actionable, function-level audit finding.
tldr: AttackPathGNN uses graph neural networks to detect cross-function vulnerabilities in smart contracts by modeling attack paths and conjunction pooling.
motivation: Existing vulnerability detectors focus on single-function patterns, missing exploits that arise from inter-function interactions.
method: The paper proposes a State Interference Graph linking functions via typed edges and a conjunction pooling aggregator that scores exploit preconditions.
result: The model achieves 92.3% F1 on SmartBugs Wild and recovers 6/10 DASP10 categories at 100% on every seed.
conclusion: AttackPathGNN provides structured remediation reports, turning predictions into actionable audit findings.

title: Adhesion-driven Rigidity Transition Decoupled From Density-driven Jamming Triggers Epithelial Organization In Embryonic Tissues

method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of cell adhesion and density in embryonic tissues.

title: Thorium-229 Lifetime Locked Down

motivation: The lifetime of the nuclear metastable state in singly charged thorium-229 ions appeared shorter than theoretical predictions, puzzling physicists for about ten years.

title: The Euclidean Algorithm, Lotuses And Singularities
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The anthyphairetic process leads from a pair (a,b) of coprime positive integers to the pair (1,1) by successive subtractions of the smaller number from the bigger one. This process, which is a slow version of Euclid's algorithm applied to the pair (a,b), corresponds naturally to the process of successive blowups leading to the minimal embedded resolution of the plane curve defined by y^a - x^b = 0. This blowup process may be represented graphically by a special two-dimensional simplicial complex called a lotus. This allows to localize the various numbers appearing either during the anthyphairetic process or during the Euclidean algorithm at precise positions inside the lotus. In this introductory article, I recall first the construction of this lotus starting from the sequence of quotients generated by the Euclidean algorithm. I present then an alternative way of constructing it directly from the sequence of pairs of coprime integers generated by the anthyphairetic process, using what I call anthyphairetic rectangles. I conclude by explaining how to reconstruct from a lotus the corresponding sequence of pairs of coprime integers. This is a simple illustration of the way lotuses may serve as computational architectures.
tldr: This paper explores the connection between the Euclidean algorithm, anthyphairetic process, and the minimal embedded resolution of plane curve singularities via a combinatorial structure called a lotus.
motivation: To provide an introductory exposition of how lotuses, derived from the Euclidean algorithm, serve as computational architectures for understanding the resolution of singularities.
method: The paper constructs a lotus from the sequence of quotients in the Euclidean algorithm and alternatively from anthyphairetic rectangles, then reconstructs the coprime pairs from the lotus.
result: The lotus structure localizes numbers from the Euclidean algorithm and anthyphairetic process, illustrating a direct correspondence with blowups in the resolution of y^a - x^b = 0.
conclusion: Lotuses offer a visual and combinatorial framework for representing the Euclidean algorithm and its geometric interpretation in singularity resolution, with potential for broader computational applications.

title: The Ize Conjecture Redux: A Parity Criterion For Global Equivariant Bifurcation Guarantees
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Ize Conjecture proposed that every absolutely irreducible representation of a compact Lie group admits a maximal isotropy subgroup with an odd-dimensional fixed-point space, which would provide a universal bifurcation guarantee via the equivariant degree. Its disproof by Lauterbach and Matthews necessitates a more targeted criterion. We introduce Ize pairs -- pairs [MATH] for which some maximal isotropy subgroup [MATH] satisfies [MATH] -- and prove that this dimension-parity condition completely captures the algebraic obstruction to a non-trivial equivariant degree change at maximal orbit types. Integrating this criterion with a mod-2 equivariant spectral flow yields local and global bifurcation guarantees without recourse to Burnside ring arithmetic. As an application, we establish unbounded branches of non-stationary periodic solutions in a [MATH]-symmetric coupled oscillator network, where the bifurcation guarantees follow entirely from the crossing parity of the linearization at the boundary of a regular parameter window.

motivation: The Ize Conjecture was disproven, so a new criterion is needed to guarantee bifurcations in equivariant systems.
method: Introduces Ize pairs and a mod-2 equivariant spectral flow to capture algebraic obstructions to nontrivial degree change.
result: The dimension-parity condition completely captures the obstruction, enabling local and global bifurcation guarantees without Burnside ring arithmetic.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for proving existence of bifurcating solutions in symmetric systems, demonstrated on a D4-symmetric oscillator network.
